## Purpose

This notebook compares binary logistic regression models for Greek river types R-M2 and R-M4 using the Akaike Information Criterion corrected for small sample size 
(AICc), to identify the most appropriate models for subsequent prediction of boundary criteria.

Models are fitted separately for the two river types using the prepared site-averaged dataset supplied in `Data/Processed/`. The preparation of this dataset is described in the repository README. All subsets of five candidate predictors are evaluated, and coefficient estimates for the retained models are reported in Table S2.

The selected models will subsequently be refitted using datasets containing only their respective predictor variables. Spatially blocked cross-validation, predictive performance and uncertainty analyses will be documented in subsequent notebooks.

## 1. Load modelling data

The five environmental predictors are phosphate, nitrate, conductivity,
dissolved oxygen and Habitat Modification Score. Phosphate, nitrate and
conductivity were log10-transformed **after averaging** in the preceding
notebook. The binary response is 1 for mean HESY2 EQR >= good moderate boundary and 0 otherwise.

```{r}

input_file <- here::here("Data", "Processed", "Greek_RM2_RM4_SiteMeans.csv")
stopifnot(file.exists(input_file))

predictors <- c("L10P_PO4", "L10N_NO3", "L10Cond", "DO", "HMS")
model_vars <- c("BinClass_HESY", predictors)
required_vars <- c("ICType", "HESY2", model_vars)

dat <- readr::read_csv(input_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
missing_vars <- setdiff(required_vars, names(dat))
if (length(missing_vars)) {
  stop("Missing required columns: ", paste(missing_vars, collapse = ", "))
}

# Use the same complete-case subset for every candidate model within a type.
# Keep site and Water District identifiers for later spatial validation.
make_model_data <- function(x, river_type) {
  x %>%
    filter(ICType == river_type, !is.na(HESY2)) %>%
    filter(if_all(all_of(model_vars), is.finite)) %>%
    as.data.frame()
}

dat_RM2 <- make_model_data(dat, "R-M2")
dat_RM4 <- make_model_data(dat, "R-M4")

# Confirm the binary response and presence of both outcome classes.
for (x in list(dat_RM2, dat_RM4)) {
  stopifnot(all(x$BinClass_HESY %in% c(0, 1)))
  stopifnot(length(unique(x$BinClass_HESY)) == 2L)
}

```



### Complete-case dataset summary

```{r dataset-summary}

print(exists("dat_RM2"))
print(exists("dat_RM4"))

sample_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dat_RM2 %>% mutate(ICType = "R-M2"),
  dat_RM4 %>% mutate(ICType = "R-M4")
) %>%
  group_by(ICType) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Good = sum(BinClass_HESY == 1),
    Not_Good = sum(BinClass_HESY == 0),
    Prevalence = mean(BinClass_HESY == 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(sample_summary)
```

## 2. Fit global models and perform all-subsets selection

The global logistic model includes all five candidate predictors without
interaction terms. The `MuMIn::dredge()` procedure ranks all subsets by AICc.
Only observations complete for the entire global model enter the comparison,
ensuring that AICc is calculated for models fitted to the same data.

The `na.action = na.fail` argument is supplied directly to `glm()`, so there
is no need to change the R session's global `na.action` option.

```{r dredge}
full_formula <- BinClass_HESY ~ L10P_PO4 + L10N_NO3 + L10Cond + DO + HMS

mod_full_RM2 <- glm(
  full_formula, data = dat_RM2,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), na.action = na.fail
)
mod_full_RM4 <- glm(
  full_formula, data = dat_RM4,
  family = binomial(link = "logit"), na.action = na.fail
)

dredge_RM2 <- MuMIn::dredge(mod_full_RM2, rank = "AICc", trace = FALSE)
dredge_RM4 <- MuMIn::dredge(mod_full_RM4, rank = "AICc", trace = FALSE)

# R-M2
cat("\n--- Dredge Results for R-M2 ---\n")
print(
  subset(
    dredge_RM2,
    delta <= 2 |
      has(L10P_PO4, !L10N_NO3, !L10Cond, !DO, !HMS),
    recalc.weights = FALSE
  )
)

# R-M4
cat("\n--- Dredge Results for R-M4 ---\n")
print(
  subset(
    dredge_RM4,
    delta <= 2 |
      has(L10P_PO4, !L10N_NO3, !L10Cond, !DO, !HMS),
    recalc.weights = FALSE
  )
)
```

```{r table-S2-data}
# Extract competitive models and the phosphorus-only model
prepare_dredge_table <- function(dredge_result, river_type) {

  selected <- subset(
    dredge_result,
    delta <= 2 |
      has(L10P_PO4, !L10N_NO3, !L10Cond, !DO, !HMS),
    recalc.weights = FALSE
  )

  tab <- as.data.frame(selected)

  # Retain model numbers from the dredge output
  tab$Model <- rownames(tab)
  tab$River_Type <- river_type

  # Select and order columns
  tab <- tab %>%
    dplyr::select(
      River_Type, Model, `(Intercept)`,
      DO, HMS, L10Cond, L10N_NO3, L10P_PO4,
      df, logLik, AICc, delta, weight
    )

  return(tab)
}

# Combine both river types
table_S2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  prepare_dredge_table(dredge_RM2, "R-M2"),
  prepare_dredge_table(dredge_RM4, "R-M4")
)

table_S2

```

This preserves the original model numbering, coefficients, AICc, ΔAICc and weights.

### Format and export using flextable

```{r}
# Identify numeric columns
stat_cols <- c(
  "(Intercept)", "DO", "HMS", "L10Cond",
  "L10N_NO3", "L10P_PO4",
  "logLik", "AICc", "delta", "weight"
)

ft_S2 <- flextable(table_S2) %>%

  # Column headings
  set_header_labels(
    River_Type = "River type",
    Model = "Model",
    `(Intercept)` = "Intercept",
    df = "df",
    logLik = "logLik",
    AICc = "AICc",
    delta = "Delta",
    weight = "Weight"
  ) %>%

  # Number formatting
  colformat_double(
    j = stat_cols,
    digits = 3,
    na_str = ""
  ) %>%

  colformat_int(j = "df") %>%

  # Table appearance
  theme_booktabs() %>%
  bold(part = "header") %>%
  merge_v(j = "River_Type") %>%
  valign(j = "River_Type", valign = "top") %>%
  align(j = stat_cols, align = "right", part = "body") %>%
  fontsize(size = 8, part = "all") %>%
  autofit()

# Display table in notebook
ft_S2

# Save as Word document
output_file <- here::here(
  "Outputs", "Tables", "Table_S2.docx"
)

dir.create(
  dirname(output_file),
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

section <- officer::prop_section(
  page_size = officer::page_size(
    orient = "landscape",
    width = 8.27,
    height = 11.69
  )
)

flextable::save_as_docx(
  "Table S2. AICc comparison of candidate logistic models" = ft_S2,
  path = output_file,
  pr_section = section
)

cat("Saved:", output_file, "\n")
```




## 3. Models retained for subsequent evaluation

The model formulas below reproduce the set considered in the paper.

- R-M2: univariate phosphate model 17 and the optimal multivariate HMS + conductivity + phosphate model 23.
- R-M4: univariate phosphate model 17, the optimal HMS + phosphate model 19 and
        additional HMS + DO + phosphate model 20.

They are re-fitted in notebook `04_Model_Evaluation.Rmd`




## Input and output

- **Input:** `Data/Processed/Greek_RM2_RM4_SiteMeans.csv`
- **Table S2:** `Outputs/Tables/Table_S2.docx`
